title: The Italian Game
blurb: Chess's oldest recorded opening, and the clearest place to learn what the first ten moves are actually for.

title: The Ruy López
blurb: The oldest opening still played at the top, and the deepest lesson in slow pressure rather than quick threats.

title: The Scotch Game
blurb: Break the centre open on move three. The clearest antidote if you find the Ruy López too slow.

title: Beating the Sicilian: the Alapin
blurb: The Sicilian is the most popular answer to 1.e4 and has a mountain of theory. 2.c3 sidesteps almost all of it.

title: The French Advance
blurb: Take space and lock the centre, then attack. The other half of a lesson about one badly placed bishop.

title: The Caro-Kann Advance
blurb: The same structure as the French, reached one move differently — and that one move solves Black's worst problem.

title: The Queen's Gambit Declined
blurb: The most respectable answer to 1.d4 in existence. Solid, principled, and unrefuted for a hundred and fifty years.

title: The Slav Defence
blurb: Decline the Queen's Gambit without burying your bishop. The same fix the Caro-Kann applies, one opening over.

title: The London System
blurb: A setup, not a line: the same five moves against almost anything Black plays. The lowest-maintenance opening in chess.

title: The King's Indian Defence
blurb: Hand White the entire centre on purpose, then blow it up. The most aggressive answer to 1.d4 there is.
